title: Duke's funeral and why Cootie stayed with Mercer
summary: The funeral recalled the Sacred Concert; Cootie calls Duke the greatest man he met and stayed on to help Mercer.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Well, that takes us to the funeral, which was a very beautiful thing. Don't you think it was?
Yeah. It was a very beautiful funeral. It brought me back to the time we played the concert there.
Yes. Yes.
The funeral did.
Yes. It sure did. It sure did. And at the very end, when they put the recording on, and up comes Alice's voice, and then Johnny --
Yeah.
-- I mean, that was -- that was like that was from up above or something, wasn't it?
Yeah.
Well, I know that -- I'm sure your feeling
is that he was the greatest musician and the greatest guy that you were ever around. I'm not putting words in your mouth, am I?
No, you're not. No, no. He was the greatest guy I ever met in life. Musician and man.
Yeah.
He really was. I never met a greater man than him.
No. No. Well, Cootie, then that was out of -- out of regard for him, I'm sure, too, that you didn't want to let Mercer down.
Oh, no.
You went out with Mercer, almost right away, didn't you?
Yeah. I went out with the band for that reason, the main reason, on account of Duke. Because I thought he needed me, and he really needed me at that time.
Yeah.

So I went on, and I think we had an interview at Johnson Publishers in Chicago. And I said -- they interviewed me -- I said the only reason I was here was on account of Duke Ellington. I had retired, and he called me and told me to come on back. I didn't have to play. Just to sit there. He missed looking at me, seeing me. And I said that's the main reason why I came back to the band. Because I
had retired and stopped blowing. I said, since he passed away, I think that Mercer needed me more than ever, so that's the reason why I'm with the band.
That's wonderful. That's wonderful. I think that's a good note for us to end this interview on. Don't you, Cootie?
Yeah. Wonderful. Thank you.
Thank you.
(End of proceedings as recorded.)
